claims.statement: Socket.IO replaces the SSE firehose with a real WebSocket (polling fallback) and an AsyncRedisManager client_manager; the server is mounted at the ASGI root in main.py after every router/middleware is registered so the construction cost stays out of test collection.

authenticate_socket_token verifies the {auth: {token}} credentials using the same get_user_from_token as REST and refuses on failure via ConnectionRefusedError; publishers route events to room conv:<conversation_id> or lead:<lead_id>, and events with neither id are suppressed (publishers must not treat None as a broadcast room).

_ConnectionAccess tracks per-SID authenticated identity (id, role), server-authorized rooms, and presence_entities / typing_entities; presence join/leave handlers call services.presence.join_viewing / leave_viewing and viewer_can_access_conversation / viewer_can_access_lead gate room membership.

The emit bridge in backend/app/realtime/emitter.py builds a write_only=True AsyncRedisManager so the bridge never starts a local server; emit_event is best-effort (every exception is swallowed and reset_manager is called on failure), and the reset-on-failure pattern guarantees the next emit builds a fresh manager bound to the current event loop after worker-chatbot's per-job asyncio.run.

The legacy SSE firehose at /realtime/* is kept as a fallback for proxies that strip the Upgrade header; Caddy uses flush_interval -1 so events flush immediately and the SSE handler reuses services.realtime.publish_event so the two transports share event sourcing.

services.realtime.publish_event is the single publishing seam: every state change funnels through it regardless of which process owns the mutation, and the recruiter console's realtime socket joins the rooms for any conversation currently in view and leaves on unmount.
